disposition_reason: Ten elements including As, Cd, Hg and Pb were measured by ICP-MS in 51 retail cheeses of nine types sold in Türkiye; Table 1 gives median (min-max) per type and the text gives overall means.

study.design: Market survey of 51 packaged cheeses (nine types), two production batches per product, with intake and THQ/HI risk assessment
study.origin: cheeses produced in Türkiye (brands sold nationally)
study.market: supermarkets, chain markets and e-commerce sites operating nationally in Türkiye
lod: LOD/LOQ in Supplementary Table 2 (not available with the PDF)
study.qa: Spike recovery on two samples at 100 µg/L; recoveries in Supplementary Table 2 (not available); no CRM reported

controls.control: cheese texture class (hard or semi-hard vs soft)
controls.outcome: Pb mean 0.08 ± 0.12 vs 0.03 ± 0.06 µg/kg; Cr 103 vs 54, Ni 199 vs 103 µg/kg; As 54.3 vs 66 µg/kg (not significant)

unresolved: LOD/LOQ and recoveries are in Supplementary Table 2, not available with the PDF.

Curd cheese Al median (467) exceeds its printed maximum (18.4); the Results text says the highest and lowest Al means were strained white cheese (8005) and curd cheese (18.4), whereas Table 1 shows 8005 as the white cheese maximum.
Discussion says about 29% of cheeses exceeded a 10 µg/kg Hg limit, but the highest Hg value printed is 0.32 µg/kg.
Medians printed as 0 are treated as below LOQ.
Per-type means are only given as ranges of means without type labels (e.g. Cr 41.5 ± 19.9 to 135 ± 122 µg/kg); not recorded as findings.
